direction: Escalate anytime-LNS effort toward the full 500 ms budget with capacity-aware adaptive ruin sizing: scale the removed-customer count to instance size and residual capacity slack (larger removals ~15-25% of n on tight-capacity/eccentric-depot instances), bias ruin selection toward the depot-distant and clustered spatial segments, and keep the accept criterion non-worsening with best-solution restart between segments.

operations.mechanism: Archive feedback shows a single-template portfolio with zero VBS gain over SBS (gap 0.0%) and all 24 wins going to the round-2 solver: the binding constraint is not diversification but raw anytime search depth. Pareto frontier mass is on the low-objective/high-time end (15.788 @ 217.7 ms), and no instance was exhausted or failed, so there is slack in the 500 ms budget that is currently being left unexploited. Weakest regimes are parameterically homogeneous (size=100, capacity tight, uniform demand, eccentric depot, clustered space at roughly -20 to -23% rel gap), which points to insufficient ruin granularity on tightly packed routes rather than a search-structure problem; a slack-aware, size-scaled removal count is the cheapest single lever inside the allowed ruin-recreate template with postprocess 'none'.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: The SBS (mean obj 15.788 at 217.7 ms) dominates the two slower variants (174.7 ms -> 16.0737, 16.1422), so within the 500 ms budget the objective is still monotonically decreasing in effective LNS iterations; therefore (a) reallocating the unused ~280 ms to additional ruin-recreate iterations and (b) making ruin size scale with residual capacity slack (bigger ruin depth on tight-capacity, clustered, eccentric-depot regimes, which are exactly the weakest factors at -20% to -23% VBS relative gap) will lower mean objective on cvrp_dev_hetero_24 by more than the round-4 best of 15.788, without any postprocess step.
